rationale: B wins because it knows when to stop. Its line, "As written, the facts honestly support three distinct angles, all gated on missing proof," is exactly the discipline this update needs. A has more inventory, but "Mercury will hold consumer deposits without holding a bank charter itself" is a dangerous banking-accuracy wobble, and "full-service bank" overstates the facts. Fewer clean angles beat five angles with two wearing borrowed clothes.
gaps_in_A: "Mercury will hold consumer deposits without holding a bank charter itself" conflicts with the supplied fact that banking services are provided through partner banks; that distinction is not copy polish, it is the story.
"mass-market consumer bank" and "full-service bank" overstate an invite-only checking-and-savings launch from a company without a bank charter.
"start narrow with businesses, expand into consumer once profitable" admits it needs another example; without that, it is an n-of-1 trend angle dressed for the runway.
"notoriously thin margins of consumer banking" imports outside economics not supplied in the update. It may be true, but it needs sourcing before becoming the spine of an angle.
gaps_in_B: "startup bank" is loose language for a company whose banking services run through partner banks, not its own charter. A fintech-regulation reporter will not let that slide.
"the same arrangement that has drawn scrutiny across consumer fintech" imports an outside scrutiny peg. Verify it or make it a question, not a stated premise.
It misses A's cleanest separate lane: Mercury's SVB-era startup-banking reputation becoming a consumer-account pitch. B uses that as setup, but does not fully exploit the brand-inversion story.
"Next step: `meanest-editor`" is the wrong handoff. Once an angle and proof are chosen, the next useful move is journalist-fit-check and target selection, not another critique loop.
